guide.summary: The final unit asks whether a process is thermodynamically favored and how that connects to equilibrium and electrochemistry. You must predict entropy changes, calculate ΔG° from ΔH° and ΔS°, relate ΔG° to K and E°, distinguish thermodynamic favorability from rate, analyze galvanic and electrolytic cells, and apply Faraday's law.

sections.heading: Entropy and Gibbs free energy
sections.body: Entropy (S) measures dispersal of matter and energy. ΔS > 0 when solids/liquids become gases, when moles of gas increase, when a solid dissolves (usually), or when temperature rises. ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° (convert ΔS° from J/K to kJ/K). ΔG° < 0: thermodynamically favored. Sign table: ΔH < 0, ΔS > 0 → favored at all T; ΔH > 0, ΔS < 0 → never; ΔH < 0, ΔS < 0 → favored at low T; ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0 → favored at high T. The crossover temperature is T = ΔH°/ΔS°.

sections.heading: Favorability, rate, and coupling
sections.body: A thermodynamically favored process may not occur at an observable rate if its activation energy is high (kinetic control): diamond converting to graphite is favored but extremely slow. Unfavorable reactions can be driven by coupling them with a favored reaction that shares an intermediate (ΔG values add), by supplying energy (light, electricity), or by removing products.

sections.heading: ΔG°, K, and E°
sections.body: ΔG° = −RT ln K: ΔG° < 0 ↔ K > 1. ΔG° = −nFE°: E° > 0 ↔ favored. When ΔG° is near zero, K is near 1 and significant amounts of both reactants and products are present at equilibrium. Under nonstandard conditions, E decreases as Q increases (Nernst equation qualitatively): increasing product ion concentration or decreasing reactant ion concentration lowers cell voltage. A cell at equilibrium has E = 0 ('dead battery').

sections.heading: Galvanic and electrolytic cells
sections.body: Galvanic cells convert chemical energy to electrical (E° > 0). Oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode; electrons flow through the wire from anode to cathode. In the salt bridge, anions migrate toward the anode and cations toward the cathode to maintain neutrality. E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) using reduction potentials; do not multiply E° by coefficients. Electrolytic cells use an external source to drive a nonspontaneous reaction. Faraday: q = It; mol e⁻ = q/F; mol metal = mol e⁻ ÷ (charge of ion).

keyTakeaways: ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° (watch J vs kJ).
Anode = oxidation; electrons flow anode → cathode.
E° is intensive: never multiply by coefficients.
commonMistakes: Mixing J and kJ in ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.
Multiplying E° values when balancing half-reactions.
Saying a favored reaction must be fast.
Forgetting n (moles of electrons) in ΔG° = −nFE°.
examTips: Expect a galvanic cell diagram in FRQs: identify anode, cathode, electron flow, and ion flow.
Justify entropy predictions with phases and moles of gas.
For 'favored but not observed', cite a high activation energy.
Electrolysis problems: track units through C → mol e⁻ → mol metal → grams.
guide.cramSheet:
**ΔS > 0:** s → l → g · more gas moles · dissolving

**ΔG:** ΔH − TΔS · < 0 favored · T = ΔH/ΔS crossover

**Links:** ΔG° = −RT ln K = −nFE° · K > 1 ↔ E° > 0

**Kinetic control:** favored but high Ea → slow

**Cells:** AN OX · RED CAT · e⁻ anode → cathode · anions → anode · E°cell = E°cat − E°an

**Nernst (qual.):** Q ↑ → E ↓ · equilibrium → E = 0

**Faraday:** q = It · mol e⁻ = q/F · F = 96,485 C/mol

vocab.definition: A measure of the dispersal of matter and energy in a system.
ΔH − TΔS; negative values indicate a thermodynamically favored process.
A process with ΔG < 0 that proceeds without continuous outside energy input.
A favored reaction that doesn't occur at a measurable rate because of a high activation energy.
An unfavorable reaction driven by a favorable one through a shared intermediate.
An electrochemical cell in which a favored redox reaction produces electric current.
An electrochemical cell driven by an external power source to cause a nonspontaneous reaction.
A connection containing ions that maintains electrical neutrality in each half-cell.
The tendency of a species to be reduced under standard conditions, in volts.
Charge of one mole of electrons: 96,485 C/mol.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Some solid Ni(NO₃)₂ is dissolved in the nickel half-cell. Predict whether the cell voltage increases, decreases, or stays the same. Justify.

rubric.description: Decreases; [Ni²⁺] is a product, so Q = [Ni²⁺]/[Ag⁺]² increases, decreasing E.

practice.sampleResponse:
(a) Ni(s) → Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻

(b) Ag⁺ is reduced at the cathode. E°cell = 0.80 − (−0.23) = 1.03 V.

(c) n = 2. ΔG° = −nFE° = −(2)(96,485 C/mol)(1.03 V) = −1.99 × 10⁵ J/mol = −199 kJ/mol.

(d) The voltage decreases. Ni²⁺ is a product of the cell reaction, so increasing [Ni²⁺] increases Q = [Ni²⁺]/[Ag⁺]². Since E decreases as Q increases, the cell potential drops below 1.03 V.
